parts.what: A smaller but consistently growing line covering crops such as tomato, beetroot, ridge gourd, sponge gourd and marigold; FY26 volumes were up modestly (about 1.5% in Q3) with revenues up 11.4%, and management groups it with rice and maize as a best-performing segment.

parts.name: Other field crops (sunflower, mustard)
parts.what: Newer additions to the portfolio — sunflower volumes grew 94% and mustard 64% in Q3 FY26, and management says mustard is expected to become a sizeable business over the next couple of years.

parts.name: Exports
parts.what: Selling seeds into international markets after registering products there over the last five years; still a small base but the fastest-growing part, with revenue up roughly 90% in FY26 (86% in Q3, 76% in Q4) and expected to keep growing.

parts.name: R&D and breeding
parts.what: The in-house research engine that creates all the hybrids the company sells — it does not use government-released seeds, but accesses germplasm from universities, government bodies and international institutes — and management calls it the backbone of the business, absorbing roughly 5%-10% of revenue including capex, alongside about Rs. 40-50 crores a year of plant/processing capex.

overview.what_it_does: Karnataka Bank is an Indian commercial bank, headquartered in Mangaluru on the Karnataka coast and founded in 1924, that takes deposits from the public and lends the money out at a higher rate — the gap between the two (net interest margin, around 2.9%-3.1% recently) is its main source of earnings, supplemented by fees and other income. It serves ordinary savers, farmers, small businesses and mid-sized companies through a branch network of over 900 branches, calling itself 'Your Family Bank, Across India'; it is strongest in Karnataka but also present in cities like Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad and Chennai, and increasingly originates and underwrites loans digitally. As of March 2026 it held about INR 1,08,779 crores of deposits and about INR 83,340 crores of loans, for total business of roughly INR 1,92,118 crores. Management's stated strategy is to grow the higher-yielding retail, agriculture and MSME book, shrink low-yielding corporate exposure, and fund itself more cheaply with current and savings accounts instead of costly bulk deposits.

parts.name: Retail, Agri and MSME (RAM)
parts.what: Loans to individuals, farmers and small businesses — housing, gold, vehicle and MSME loans are the named growth drivers — and management calls this 'the core driver of our growth strategy', at INR 51,197 crores of the INR 83,340 crores loan book as of March 2026, or roughly 60%.

parts.name: Corporate and mid-corporate advances
parts.what: Lending to mid-sized and large companies, including loans taken on opportunistically when they paid better than parking money in treasury; the bank is deliberately rationalising this book, cutting low-yielding exposure while growing mid-corporate (up ~13% in Q4 FY26) with better-quality, better-yielding names.

parts.name: Deposits / liabilities (CASA, retail term, bulk)
parts.what: The funding side of the bank — current and savings accounts (CASA) at 33.61% of deposits, or INR 36,559 crores, plus retail term deposits under INR 3 crores at INR 67,648 crores — with an explicit push to raise CASA and cut high-cost bulk deposits (down to 4.2% of total deposits) to keep funding costs low.

parts.name: Branch banking and retail network
parts.what: The physical distribution arm of over 900 branches, run as its own vertical alongside a dedicated retail advances vertical, and supported by retail credit hubs (expanded from 3 towards 8) that process loans up to about INR 2.5 crores.

parts.name: Treasury / investments
parts.what: The bank's portfolio of government and other securities, which generates investment income and trading profit and is the alternative use of funds against corporate lending; RBI's investment accounting change in FY25 routed some gains to an 'AFS Reserve' rather than through profit.

parts.name: Government and transaction business
parts.what: Collection of taxes, GST and customs duty and, via integration with the Karnataka government's Khajane-II treasury system, government challan receipts — pursued mainly as a way to bring in low-cost balances rather than as a large standalone earner.

parts.name: Third-party products and fee income
parts.what: Sale of bundled and partner products such as insurance top-ups on the KBL WISE senior-citizen deposit, overseen by a Head of Liabilities Sales and Third-Party Products; contributes to 'other income', which was INR 1,155.50 crores in FY23.

parts.name: Digital origination and technology
parts.what: In-house digital lending and platform build-out, described as underwriting about 85% of originated loans digitally as of 2023, with the technology budget raised roughly 80% that year and new products and platforms still being rolled out.

parts.name: Recovery and asset quality management
parts.what: Dedicated credit monitoring, recovery and provisioning effort to clean up bad loans — gross NPAs were brought down to 2.78% and net NPAs to 0.98% by March 2026, with provision coverage built back up through accelerated provisioning.
